races.name: Racing TV Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lumenbourg
runners_data.note: Front runner with 22 days since last run and amateur rider aboard, vulnerable if pace becomes testing
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins have been at 7f, although has plenty of good runs at 6f; good third to a subsequent winner at Redcar last time (6f, good); should go well.

runners_data.name: Groundsman
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making stable debut for Mark Loughnane, should improve significantly on Lingfield effort
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner for Richard Fahey (7f); well beaten on stable debut after a break on turf at Lingfield last month (7f, good) but should come on for the outing; first run on soft ground.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over course and distance last year, these soft conditions suit perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D in May last year (good to soft); beaten 7l when third at Ripon last week (6f, good); these are his ideal conditions and should go well.

runners_data.name: Andalprofit
runners_data.note: Prominent type coming off a win but on firmer ground, soft going represents unknown quantity
runners_data.spotlight: Won for today's rider off a 2lb lower mark at Redcar last time (6f, good to firm); today's softer conditions are not sure to suit.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form but up 10lb from last win, soft ground concern given recent firm ground victories
runners_data.spotlight: Comes into this in good form having won over 6f at Ayr (good to firm) and Ripon (good) last month; up 10lb (5lb higher than last time) and a contender, but softer ground a concern.

runners_data.name: Amaysmont
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer better on all-weather, lowest-rated runner but well-handicapped on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Better on the AW, but better handicapped on turf; fair third at Southwell two runs back (7f), but modest efforts either side of that; this softer ground no problem.

races.paceDynamic: Lumenbourg will take the race along from the gates with his confirmed front-running style, likely getting an uncontested lead in this small field. Bay Breeze and Andalprofit will track in prominent positions behind the leader, while the three hold-up horses Groundsman, Jet Warrior and Amaysmont will need to come from off the pace. With soft ground likely to emphasize stamina over speed and only one true pace-setter, this sets up perfectly for horses that can settle and deliver a sustained finish. This race shape strongly favours hold-up performers and late closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground emphasizes stamina and the pace becomes steady rather than testing
scenarios.body: Lumenbourg's modest early gallop allows the closers time to wind up their finishing kicks on ground that rewards sustained effort over speed. Groundsman and Jet Warrior benefit most from being able to use their class from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Breeze and Andalprofit can position ideally just behind Lumenbourg and kick clear
scenarios.body: The duo get first run on the field from their tracking positions while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on the testing surface. Bay Breeze's course and distance win and Andalprofit's current form prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg gets too easy a lead and the field fails to close him down
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage through fractions that are too comfortable, with the soft ground sapping the finishing kicks of his pursuers. His 6f form and fitness edge prove enough to repel late challenges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Lumenbourg goes too slow early then quickens dramatically turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the horses with the highest cruising speed benefit most from the lack of early pace. Jet Warrior's recent winning form and Andalprofit's speed become crucial in a dash to the line.

watchPoints.text: Lumenbourg getting too easy a lead early with no pressure from the small field behind
Groundsman's fitness levels after disappointing stable debut following a break from racing
Jet Warrior handling the significant weight rise after consecutive wins on much firmer surfaces
Bay Breeze's ability to replicate course and distance form from 12 months ago
The pace development with only one confirmed front runner in a six-horse field

races.name: Watch Racing TV Live EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Blakey Ridge
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 105,000euros yearling; first foal; by Sioux Nation out of unraced half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Emaraaty Ana, out of 1m4f Listed winner; yard's 2yos can go well first time but 1-29 with them here.

runners_data.name: Excessive
runners_data.spotlight: May foal; 15,000euros foal; eighth foal; Cotai Glory gelded half-brother to winners Dorian Gray (1m2f-1m4f AW; RPR 65) and Flosrose (Italian 1m 2yo); dam 6f AW 2yo winner (97); a late foal who may need more time; yard also runs Kaiulani Spirit.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £16,000 yearling; ninth foal; gelded son of Caturra out of mare who won on debut for another yard (5f; RPR 94) and produced winners including Flyin Hawaiian (10.6f AW; RPR 82) and Oahu (6f AW 2yo; 77); market can guide regarding this one and stablemate Excessive.

runners_data.name: Mangham
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; by Harry Angel; tenth foal; half-brother to winners Akeed Dubawi (1m AW; RPR 80), Tarnhelm (6f-1m; 72) and Billy McGarry (7f-8.6f, mostly AW; 66); dam 5f 2yo winner (90); has been gelded; jumps trainer combination's first 2yo runner; likely other days.

runners_data.name: Rock Steady Beat
runners_data.spotlight: 110,000gns yearling; dam's winning offspring include Happy Romance, a Group 3 winner as 2yo and 3yo; 6-1 for York debut (6f, good) and he showed up well for a long way in a stronger race than this; can improve; good claims dropped to 5f.

runners_data.name: Eevee Star
runners_data.spotlight: Dam excelled on very soft ground when winning a French Listed race (5f) as 2yo; 15-2 for Ripon debut (6f, good) when soon well adrift but she did some good late work into third of eight; ought to progress and the drop in trip on today's stiff track shouldn't hold her back too much.

runners_data.name: Sydney Grace
runners_data.spotlight: Never near the leaders on Yarmouth debut (5f, good; 16-1) but signs of ability even so, albeit she swished her tail when asked to improve; may well do better for yard that's 1-5 with 2yos here.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Dream
runners_data.spotlight: 38,000gns breeze-up 2yo; 9-1 for recent 5f debut at Redcar where he was never involved after starting slowly but hinted at some ability despite running green; should improve, perhaps when handicapping.

races.name: Follow Racing TV On X Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Glory Road
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strongest form credentials returning from 25-day break for top-class connections
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up at Nottingham (8.3f, good to soft) last October on sole 2yo start and again showed considerable promise when third at Newbury (1m2f, good) last month; he's the one to beat on form.

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.note: Promising prominent type who may have been unsuited by fast ground last time, better tactical position expected
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second when 16-1 on debut at Thirsk (1m, good) in April; perhaps unsuited by the fast ground (hung right) when 8l fourth of seven at Hamilton (1m1f, good to firm) a fortnight ago; holds each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Snake Hips
runners_data.note: Expensive hold-up debutant from strong stable but faces tactical disadvantage with limited early pace
runners_data.spotlight: 25,000gns foal; twelfth foal; half-brother to five winners including Staxton (6f; RPR 106; for this yard), Lazarus Bell (7f 2yo; 89), Classic Pursuit (prolific 5f/6f; 89) and Satin Snake (7f AW; 81); dam 1m4f winner (80); likely to improve for this debut run but could give a good account.

runners_data.name: Steel Raven
runners_data.note: Well-bought newcomer needing to overcome hold-up style in race lacking genuine tempo
runners_data.spotlight: £52,000 yearling, 87,000euros 2yo breeze-ups; second foal; half-brother to 7f winner We've Got This (RPR 69); unraced dam from useful family; the betting could be informative on debut.

runners_data.name: Affettuoso
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 185-day absence but form at Wolverhampton reads well for this grade
runners_data.spotlight: Improved from his debut run at Doncaster (1m, soft) when runner-up at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) last December at 5-6; that latest form reads well and there can be optimism that this well-bred 3yo can continue to progress for his respected Newmarket trainer; key player.

runners_data.name: Sodeto
runners_data.note: Only genuine front runner with tongue-tie fitted, faded badly in bumper debut but different tactics expected
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who was tailed off at 40-1 in a bumper at Haydock (1m7f, good) on last month's debut; a tongue-tie replaces a hood; probably best watched.

runners_data.name: Vintage Marsala
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 290-day break with minimal form credentials to work with
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has some potential in his pedigree but he was always in last place when 12-1 for his debut at Redcar (1m, good to firm) last August; needs to be an entirely different proposition on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Sanny Doo
runners_data.note: Limited hold-up horse whose sprint form suggests this trip may be too far
runners_data.spotlight: He's achieved very little across his three starts (6f/5f).

runners_data.name: Lorton Valley
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has achieved little in two AW starts and faces stronger opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten in fifth earlier this year on his first two starts (1m, AW) and he has plenty to find if he's to be competitive today.

runners_data.name: Turret
runners_data.note: Expensive hold-up debutant who ran green on debut but breeding suggests improvement possible
runners_data.spotlight: 17-2, ran green when beaten a long way on last month's debut at Lingfield (1m, AW); a dramatic transformation is needed but he cost 580,000euros in 2024 and his dam is from an excellent family; should be capable of considerably better at some point.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Weak hold-up type making little appeal on poor debut showing at longer odds
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who was 66-1 when always behind and well beaten on last month's debut at Ayr (6f, good to firm); likely he's one for further down the line.

runners_data.name: Sun Lord
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs significant improvement despite showing some ability over longer trips
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown ability on both starts (1m3f/1m2f, good to soft/good to firm) and he could have more to offer, but a sizeable step forward is needed.

runners_data.name: Ceinture d'Orion
runners_data.note: Prominent type with decent debut form who should appreciate the likely steady early tempo
runners_data.spotlight: 9-2 when fourth of seven, beaten just over 5l, on debut in warm novice at Wetherby (1m2f, good to firm) in April; well beaten at Haydock (1m2f, soft) since and has something to prove on slow ground, but she's an each-way contender if rediscovering her initial promise.

races.paceDynamic: Sodeto appears the only confirmed front runner in this 13-runner field, likely to set a sustainable pace without early pressure given most rivals are prominent/hold-up types. Glory Road, Pepsea, Affettuoso and Ceinture d'Orion will likely track just behind in the prominent positions, with the large contingent of hold-up horses including Snake Hips, Steel Raven and Turret settling towards the rear. The lack of genuine pace pressure should create a tactical affair with the real racing beginning late in the straight. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to strike when the pace lifts, while pure hold-up horses face a significant disadvantage with limited early pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of early pace allows prominent horses to position ideally behind Sodeto
scenarios.body: Glory Road and Affettuoso can utilise their class advantage from perfect stalking positions, while Pepsea and Ceinture d'Orion also benefit from being close to a moderate tempo. The hold-up brigade will find insufficient pace to run at and struggle to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debut Winners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the expensive debutants Snake Hips or Steel Raven possess the ability their price tags suggest
scenarios.body: One of the newcomers could overcome the tactical disadvantage through sheer class, with Snake Hips having strong stable form and Steel Raven representing connections with a good recent record. They'll need to be exceptionally talented to win from hold-up positions in this race shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Sodeto sets an even slower tempo than expected and the field comes together late
scenarios.body: The superior class of Glory Road and potentially Turret (expensive purchase) could prove decisive in a sprint finish where early positioning matters less. This would require the pace to be genuinely crawling to negate the prominent runners' advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Sodeto improves dramatically from his poor bumper debut and maintains a strong gallop
scenarios.body: The lack of other pace angles could allow him to steal a march on better-fancied rivals who may not respond quickly enough to his move. His tongue-tie replacement for hood suggests connections expect improvement.

watchPoints.text: Snake Hips and Steel Raven in betting markets as expensive debutants could reveal genuine ability despite tactical concerns
Glory Road's market position given his superior form but 25-day absence and need to confirm soft ground handling
Early positioning of Sodeto and whether he actually goes forward or gets shuffled back by more prominent types
Turret's improvement from debut given his substantial purchase price and potential for dramatic progress
How aggressively the prominent runners Pepsea and Ceinture d'Orion position themselves behind the leaders

races.name: racingtv.com Handicap

runners_data.name: The Bell Conductor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent soft ground form, Jason Hart excels tactically, tongue-tie application suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran; goes well on soft ground and ran a fine race when second to Trilby (2lb worse off for 0.5l) at Haydock last time (5f, soft; tongue-tie tried); tongue-tie retained and sound each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Station X
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who thrives on soft/heavy ground, Bryan Smart 0/11 record concerning but horse has individual class edge
runners_data.spotlight: All his wins have been at 6f, the latest at Southwell in April, but effective at 5f; goes particularly well on soft/heavy ground so today's conditions should be ideal; fair run last time at Hamilton (1.25l sixth of 13); could go well from his high draw.

runners_data.name: Francisco's Piece
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 62-day break with Listed class on soft ground as juvenile, needs pace to develop
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins over 5f on soft/heavy as a juvenile, the second a Listed event at Chantilly; hasn't won since and only seventh of nine on reappearance, but on a fair mark; could go well though stall 1 a slight negative.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Recent 5f soft ground winner but hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage, cheekpieces boost worked last time at Haydock
runners_data.spotlight: Had his ideal conditions when gaining his fourth win at Haydock last month (5f, soft) when wearing cheekpieces for the first time; solid third of 20 off this 5lb higher mark at York last time (5f, good; fifth has won since); stall 2 perhaps not ideal but one with a chance.

runners_data.name: Spoof
runners_data.note: Veteran 5f specialist ideally suited by conditions but 72-day absence and age concerns, needs strong gallop to be effective
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran; all 12 wins have been over 5f and is ideally suited by plenty of give in the ground; hasn't been out since Doncaster win in March (5f, good to soft); has plenty in his favour and should go well again.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent 5f record just five days after Hamilton win, Jack Nicholls 5lb claim valuable asset
runners_data.spotlight: Has won ten of his 50 races on the Flat, all over 5f, the latest on his reappearance at Hamilton (good) last week; goes well on soft/heavy ground; another good run on the cards.

runners_data.name: Hundred Caps
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but limited soft ground experience, visor application suggests handling issues may persist
runners_data.spotlight: Suited by 5f on a stiff track (two of his three wins have been at Beverley); fair fifth at Beverley with a visor tried last time (5f, good; pulled hard); regular cheekpieces back on here but soft ground a negative.

runners_data.name: Peter The Wolf
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with only one career win, Warren Greatrex runners often need time to find form, tactical disadvantage
runners_data.spotlight: Only win was a 6f Chepstow maiden last September (6f, soft; 8-15 favourite); well beaten both starts since; bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Arctic Summer
runners_data.note: Ex-French hold-up performer needing cheekpieces to show best form, moderate recent efforts suggest decline
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; only win was over 6f at Chantilly as a juvenile (very soft); not been in top form this season and needs cheekpieces to have a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.spotlight: Four of his five wins have been on the AW and has plenty to find with Trilby, who beat him by 6l at Haydock last time (5f, soft).

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form disappoints but soft ground conditions ideal, good draw provides tactical hope
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't been at his best since winning at Ripon early last month (5f, good); today's conditions ideal and could bounce back from good draw.

runners_data.name: Qila
runners_data.note: Unexposed handicap debutant with promise but unproven on testing ground, likely to need this experience
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed handicap debutant; best run when second in a 5f Newcastle novice last time; could go well but unproven on soft ground and this looks competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Station X represents the sole confirmed front-runner in this field and should be able to dictate terms without early pressure from the stalls. The Bell Conductor and Parisiac are likely to track just behind, with prominent runners like Hundred Caps and Vince L'Amour settling handy, while the majority including Trilby, Francisco's Piece, Spoof and Peter The Wolf will be held up in the pack. With only one horse committed to making the running over this minimum trip on testing ground, Station X can control the gallop and create a tactical advantage. This pace setup strongly favours horses with early pace who can position prominently and avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will emerge in the final furlong scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Station X gets an easy lead and controls the fractions.
scenarios.body: Station X can dictate his own terms without pressure and has proven 5f ability on soft ground conditions. The hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground on the testing surface against a horse who has everything his own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Success
scenarios.trigger: If The Bell Conductor or Parisiac can track Station X and outkick him late.
scenarios.body: The prominent horses get the perfect tow into the race and can use their tactical speed advantage over the hold-up brigade. Soft ground will make it harder for back-markers to close effectively over this sharp 5f trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the ground plays more fairly than expected.
scenarios.body: Trilby and Spoof both have proven 5f soft ground form and could benefit if the early leaders go too fast or tire dramatically. However, they need significant pace collapse to be effective from their likely positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Competitive Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Station X gets pressed early or doesn't handle the ground as expected.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses arrive together in the final furlong creating a blanket finish where draw and racing luck become crucial. The testing conditions could level the playing field between different running styles.

watchPoints.text: Station X could get an uncontested lead if no other pace materiates early and dominate throughout
The Bell Conductor and Parisiac positioning in the first furlong will determine if they can track the leader effectively
Trilby needs significant early pace to set up his hold-up style on this sharp 5f trip
Spoof returning from 72-day absence may need the run despite ideal conditions
Draw positions for the prominent runners could prove crucial in this 12-runner field on Carlisle's tight track

races.name: Join Racing TV Now Handicap

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making soft ground debut after fair third at Ripon, needs to prove surface effectiveness
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden; some fair runs on the Flat this year, notably when third at Ripon last time (1m4f, good); first run on soft ground.

runners_data.name: West Tyrone
runners_data.note: Front-runner with AW form returning after 44-day break, proven at trip but needs to transfer form to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Kevin Ryan; won a 1m AW handicap in March 2025; stays 1m2f but below-par when tried over further; bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Jaminoz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with C&D soft ground win, strong record on give in ground makes him major player
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time winner, including over C&D last July (good to soft); well suited by give in the ground, so after two fair runs this season, is one with a chance.

runners_data.name: Golspie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with soft ground form, three fair runs in March suggest he's ready to strike
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins have been at 1m/1m2f, one on soft ground; three fair runs in March (all over 1m2f, two on AW, the other on good to soft); hampered when a well-beaten third last time; could go well if as effective on softer ground and over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid recent C&D second, lacks consistency but well-positioned tactically
runners_data.spotlight: Not the best of strike-rates but two sound runs this season, latest when runner-up over C&D 11 days (good); could go well but not particularly consistent; softer ground no problem.

runners_data.name: Taylormade Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and C&D winner, two fair runs this season suggest he's primed
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner last August (good to firm) who was subsequently runner-up at Hamilton (1m4f, soft); two fair runs this time, latest over C&D; chance.

runners_data.name: V Twelve
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 62-day break including chase runs, needs to bounce back from poor efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile; soundly beaten on both starts this year (1m4f Catterick handicap, 1m7f Hexham handicap chase); needs to bounce back, but has a chance on his form on the Flat last year; soft going not a problem.

runners_data.name: Dr Rio
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose six wins all came at Beverley, needs to prove he can transfer form
runners_data.spotlight: All six wins in Britain have been at Beverley, the latest over 7.5f last August (good); has also won at up to 1m4f there so has a chance following good run last time; soft ground a slight concern.

runners_data.name: Scotland The Brave
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 405-day layoff following wind operation, best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle in February last year (2m); back after a wind op but probably best watched after 405-day break.

runners_data.name: Junkyard Dog
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 311-day break, handles soft ground but needs fitness edge
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish; fair hurdler; only Flat win was over 1m2f at Navan in April 2025 (good); handles soft ground; not out of it.

runners_data.name: Letmeseethecolts
runners_data.note: Prominent runner well beaten after long break last time, has bit to prove on return to form
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice last year, second time over 1m4f at Pontefract in April (good); well beaten after 380-day break last time and has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Dubai Venture
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse moving up in trip after good Pontefract second, needs to prove stamina at distance
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over 1m4f on good to firm last season; began the season with a good second at Pontefract last month (1m4f, good to soft) and could go well if coping with this softer ground.

races.paceDynamic: West Tyrone and V Twelve are the confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, with V Twelve particularly keen and West Tyrone having proven pace from his AW success. Jaminoz, Taylormade Lad and Letmeseethecolts will sit prominently behind the leaders, creating a solid pace through the early stages. The soft ground and 1m3f trip will favour sustained galloping rather than sprint finishes, suiting horses with tactical speed who can position handy and kick. This pace setup clearly favours prominent runners and hold-up horses with a turn of foot over pure front-runners who may pay for early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Honest Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone and V Twelve engage in a genuine pace battle from the off
scenarios.body: The even tempo plays into the hands of horses who can travel smoothly in behind and finish strongly. Hold-up horses like Golspie, Naturalia and Dr Rio get the run-shape they need to deliver their best efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Jaminoz and Taylormade Lad position perfectly behind the leaders and dictate
scenarios.body: The C&D winner Jaminoz uses his soft ground form while Taylormade Lad employs his course knowledge to dominate from ideal positions. Their tactical positioning neutralises the pure hold-up horses who get too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too steady early allowing the field to bunch
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace brings stamina into play over the extended trip, favouring horses who stay strongly. Dubai Venture and Junkyard Dog benefit from the searching test while speed horses struggle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If West Tyrone gets an uncontested lead and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: His proven AW winning form transfers to this surface as he controls the race tactically. V Twelve fades from pressing while the hold-up brigade leave themselves too much to do.

watchPoints.text: V Twelve could set suicidal fractions if over-keen on return from mixed campaign including chase runs
Scotland The Brave returning from 405-day break after wind surgery makes him a complete unknown quantity
Watch Jaminoz's position early as his C&D soft ground win makes him the one to beat if handy
Monitor if West Tyrone gets uncontested lead as his tactical speed could prove decisive
Dubai Venture stepping up significantly in trip after 1m4f efforts, stamina unproven at this distance

races.name: Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who will dictate terms from the start with Daniel Tudhope booking suggesting confidence despite poor recent form
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 and hasn't progressed but ran respectably when third of six in Nottingham handicap (1m2f, good) last Wednesday; has run well on good to soft (unraced on softer); could have a part to play.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who impressed on handicap debut here on soft ground and benefits from step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on handicap debut here (1m, soft) last month and the drop back to 7f looked to be against him at Leicester (good to firm) eight days later, when he stayed on for third; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Lightening Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 29-day break with Grant Tuer's small stable in good form recently
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for encouraging second on debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) last November; yet to build on that on his two runs since (1m/7f, AW/good) but his pedigree suggests the extra yardage could be a plus on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Clocker
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 50-day absence but showed promise before fading in her last three starts
runners_data.spotlight: She's raced three times and she showed up well before fading into fourth on her reappearance in a maiden at Newcastle (1m, AW) in April; her pedigree indicates this extra furlong will be a positive on her handicap debut and she's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Attention Seeker
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent Beverley fourth suggests she's returning to form after disappointing sequence
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 and had been regressive this year, but last month's fourth of nine at Beverley (1m2f, good to firm) was a step back in the right direction; ran well on soft ground last September and he's not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Espanita
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced prominent runner who hasn't built on Wolverhampton win but remains capable on her day
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in March on second start; she remains lightly raced and is not written off but she's failed to progress since that win and was only eighth of 12 on last month's turf debut (8.3f, good to soft).

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won after gelding operation but faded badly last time over longer trip at Haydock
runners_data.spotlight: Having been gelded he made a winning handicap and seasonal debut at Redcar (1m, good to firm) in April; only fifth at Haydock (1m2f, good to soft) since but faded late on and he could be in the mix over a furlong shorter.

runners_data.name: Mr Moonshine
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making seasonal return after 265-day break which makes him hard to assess
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for neck second on nursery debut at Thirsk (1m, good) last September; soundly beaten at Beverley (8.4f, soft) 11 days later and he's unproven on slow ground, but he reappears having been gelded and remains one to be interested in given the Thirsk effort.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has struggled this season and tends to fade in the finish according to his profile
runners_data.spotlight: Best 2yo run came when keeping on for close fourth here (6f, good) in September; however, he's struggled elsewhere on both runs this season (7.4f/7f, good to soft/AW) and a dramatic revival is needed back at Carlisle.

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to a few winners and a market check is advised in this second handicap; however, he was soundly beaten at 50-1 in mid-division in a handicap at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last month; improvement needed.

runners_data.name: Scheffler
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching to Adrian Nicholls and making first turf appearance after moderate all-weather efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third on debut at Lingfield (7f, AW) in March before two lesser runs (6f/1m, AW); has since left Richard Hughes; interesting to see how he goes in the betting in first-time cheekpieces on handicap/stable debut.

runners_data.name: Ibn Altheeb
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trying first-time blinkers but has struggled on turf compared to all-weather form
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) last October in first-time cheekpieces and he's one to watch in the betting in first-time blinkers today, but he's struggled on both runs this season and a major turnaround is necessary.

races.paceDynamic: Unchartedterritory will likely take the lead from the start with little early pressure, creating a sustainable gallop rather than fierce fractions. The majority of this field comprises hold-up horses (Hatamoto, Clocker, Ephron, Mr Moonshine, Cosmic Man, Scheffler, Ibn Altheeb) who will settle behind the pace, while prominent racers like Lightening Lad, Attention Seeker and Espanita track the leader without applying significant pressure. With soft ground potentially stretching the finish and most runners needing to come from behind, this tactical setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will emerge in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Unchartedterritory maintains an uncontested lead and kicks clear entering the straight
scenarios.body: The soft ground will blunt the finishing speed of hold-up horses while the leader enjoys first run on the rail. Those tracking prominently like Lightening Lad and Espanita can follow through but the pace-setter proves hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes modest and prominent racers can position ideally to strike
scenarios.body: Horses like Lightening Lad and Attention Seeker can time their challenges perfectly from good positions while late closers get caught too far back. The soft ground aids stamina types who don't have to use up energy making ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the middle stages to set up a strong finish
scenarios.body: The genuine pace allows class horses like Ephron and Hatamoto to show their ability with well-timed runs from off the pace. Soft conditions help stamina over speed as they unleash sustained challenges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Unchartedterritory goes too slow early and creates a bunched field turning for home
scenarios.body: A messy finish develops where positioning and luck in running become crucial factors. Any horse finding clear room can capitalise but it becomes a lottery with multiple chances.
